title: How do equals and hashCode work together?
keyPoints: Equal objects must return the same hashCode (the contract)
Overriding equals without hashCode breaks HashMap/HashSet lookups
Use Objects.equals and Objects.hash for null-safe implementations
equals must be reflexive, symmetric, transitive, and consistent

title: What makes an object immutable?
keyPoints: All fields private and final, set only in the constructor
No setters or other mutating methods
Defensive copies for mutable fields like arrays, Date, collections
Don't leak internal mutable references through getters
Class itself final, or otherwise prevents subclasses from breaking invariants

title: Explain HashMap internals
keyPoints: Backed by an array of buckets (Node<K,V>[])
hash() spreads bits to reduce collisions
Collisions handled with a linked list, treeified to a red-black tree after 8 entries (Java 8+)
Load factor (default 0.75) triggers resize and rehashing, capacity doubles
Not thread-safe; use ConcurrentHashMap for concurrent access

title: When would you use Optional?
keyPoints: Represents a possibly-absent return value, avoids null checks
Avoid using Optional for fields, parameters, or serialization
Prefer map/filter/orElse over isPresent() + get()
Never call get() without checking presence first

title: How do Java generics work?
keyPoints: Type erasure removes generic type info at runtime, replaced with bounds or Object
Bounded types (extends/super) restrict allowed type parameters
PECS: producer extends, consumer super, for wildcard usage
Cannot create generic arrays directly
Unchecked warnings arise because generics aren't enforced at runtime

title: How do streams differ from collections?
keyPoints: Streams describe a computation pipeline, not a data structure
Streams are lazy: intermediate ops (filter/map) don't run until a terminal op
Streams can be infinite; collections are always finite
A stream can only be consumed once

title: Explain CompletableFuture
keyPoints: Represents the result of an async computation, supports composition
thenApply/thenCompose chain transformations; thenCombine/allOf/anyOf combine futures
exceptionally/handle provide async exception handling
Runs on ForkJoinPool.commonPool by default unless an Executor is supplied
Avoids blocking Future.get() and callback-hell patterns

title: What lives on the JVM heap?
keyPoints: Objects and arrays live on the heap; instance variables included
Heap is split into young generation (eden, survivor) and old generation
Local variables and call frames live on the stack, not the heap
Class metadata lives in metaspace (off-heap since Java 8)

title: How does garbage collection work?
keyPoints: Mark-and-sweep: find objects reachable from GC roots, reclaim the rest
Generational hypothesis: most objects die young, so young gen is collected frequently
Minor GC (young gen) is cheap; major/full GC (old gen) is expensive
Collectors like G1, ZGC, Parallel trade off pause time vs throughput
finalize() is deprecated; prefer try-with-resources or Cleaner

title: How do you test concurrent code?
keyPoints: Use CountDownLatch/CyclicBarrier to coordinate threads deterministically
Stress test with many iterations/thread counts to surface race conditions
Avoid Thread.sleep for synchronization; use proper await mechanisms
Test for both correctness (no data races) and liveness (no deadlocks)
